meta.title: Persistent heartburn and regurgitation
meta.candidate_brief: You are the junior doctor in the gastroenterology clinic. Take a focused history from this patient who has been referred by their GP with upper abdominal discomfort.

patient_script.opening_statement: Doctor, this burning in my chest just won't quit.

if_asked.symptom_details: It's a burning feeling behind my breastbone that sometimes brings up sour fluid into my mouth.
if_asked.timing: It started about four months ago and happens most days, especially after dinner.
if_asked.after_effects: I feel bloated and a bit nauseous after an episode.
if_asked.exacerbating: Large, late meals and lying down too soon make it worse.
if_asked.relieving: Sipping water and taking the over-the-counter antacid help a little.
if_asked.associated_symptoms: I sometimes get a dry cough at night but no vomiting, black stools, or trouble swallowing.
if_asked.past_medical_history: I have mild asthma since childhood and seasonal allergies.
if_asked.medications: I use my blue inhaler occasionally and recently started taking chewable antacids after meals.
if_asked.allergies: I'm allergic to penicillin; it gave me a rash as a kid.
if_asked.family_history: My dad has high blood pressure; no stomach problems that I know of.
if_asked.social_history: I don't smoke, drink a glass of wine on weekends, live with my wife, and work as an accountant. I don't use drugs.
if_asked.functional_status: I still go to work, but the heartburn keeps me up at night and I'm tired the next day.

collateral.observer_note: Spouse says patient wakes up coughing from acid taste.

patient_script.emotional_tone: Slightly anxious, rubs chest when describing symptoms.

patient.name: Alex Morgan
patient.baseline_body_language: Leaning forward, hand on upper abdomen

pc.one_liner: I've had this burning feeling in my chest for months now.

hpc.timing: Worse in evenings and after meals
hpc.exacerbating: Large meals, late eating, lying flat

ice.concerns: Worried it might turn into something serious
ice.expectations: Hopes for stronger medicine or advice
